britannica-1911-abu-bekr:
Abu-Bekr (573-634) was the first caliph, the successor who led the Muslim community after Muhammad's death. Born at Mecca, a wealthy merchant of the Koreish tribe, he gained the name Abu-Bekr through his daughter Ayesha's marriage to Muhammad. His early conversion mattered greatly, and his devotion earned him the title El Siddik, the faithful.

Succession came with crisis. Abu-Bekr put down revolts in the Hejaz and Nejd, and his general Khalid defeated the rival prophet Mosailima at Akraba. Once Arabia was subdued, his armies moved into Persian Irak and Syria. Fearing the prophet's sayings would be lost, Omar urged their collection in writing, the record that later fed into the Koran.
